static.description: A Spring Boot Kotlin application providing a REST API for managing travel trips (CRUD operations) with JPA persistence and H2 in-memory database.
domain_concepts: Trip: The core JPA entity representing a travel trip with attributes like title, description, destination, and date range, persisted in the 'trips' table.
TripDto: A data transfer object used for creating and updating trips via the REST API, with validation constraints (e.g., title must not be blank).
TripService: The service layer that encapsulates business logic for CRUD operations on Trip entities, using transactional boundaries.
TripRepository: A Spring Data JPA repository interface providing standard CRUD database operations for the Trip entity.
TripController: The REST controller exposing /api/trips endpoints for listing, getting, creating, updating, and deleting trips.

dynamic.architecture_summary: A standard layered Spring Boot application following Controller → Service → Repository architecture. The project uses Spring Modulith for modular structure, JPA with H2 for persistence, and exposes a RESTful CRUD API for Trip entities. Docker Compose support is included via spring-boot-docker-compose for local development.

agent_safe_operations: Add new REST endpoints in existing or new controllers
Add new service methods in TripService or new service classes
Add new DTOs in the dto package
Add new entity classes in the model package
Add new repository interfaces in the repository package
Add or modify unit and integration tests
Modify application.properties or application.yml for non-secret configuration
agent_forbidden_operations: Modify or delete Gradle wrapper files (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/)
Add secrets, API keys, or credentials to any source file or configuration
Change the database strategy from H2 to a production database without explicit instruction
Modify settings.gradle.kts project name or structure
Delete existing test files without replacement
potential_pitfalls: The project uses Spring Boot 4.0.4 which is a very recent/bleeding-edge version — some libraries or plugins may not be fully compatible.
Kotlin data classes as JPA entities require special care: the Trip entity uses 'var' for mutable fields and a nullable id with GenerationType.IDENTITY, which is intentional.
The DGS codegen plugin is configured but no GraphQL schema files exist yet under src/main/resources/graphql-client — the generateJava task may fail if invoked without schemas.
Both application.properties and application.yml exist — Spring Boot will load both, and properties in one may override the other in unexpected ways.
The @field:NotBlank annotation in TripDto uses Kotlin's annotation use-site target — omitting 'field:' would place the annotation on the constructor parameter instead, breaking validation.
GraalVM native image plugin is configured — native compilation has additional constraints on reflection and dynamic proxies that may break new features.
The Kotlin compiler option '-Xannotation-default-target=param-property' affects how annotations are applied by default, which can impact JPA and validation annotations.
